source: Karnataka NMMS MAT 2020-21 question paper, NMMS-MAT (K-8) P-1 (pyq/NMMSMATQP202021.pdf). The paper has no answer key, so every answer here is worked out by us.

sections.directions: Complete the following number series by choosing the correct number from the given alternatives.
The order of the letters that needs to come in the boxes to complete a certain pattern is:
Complete the given analogy by selecting the correct answer from alternatives.
Identify the wrong number / pair of numbers in the given series.
Four groups of numbers / pair of numbers / group of letters are given for each question, of which three of them are alike and one is different. Select the different one.
The following Venn diagrams show the relationship among the three given objects. Identify the appropriate diagram to show the relationship among them.
Find the missing number/letter in the given matrices.
Choose and substitute the correct set of signs in place of * sequentially, selecting from the given alternatives, to make the equation meaningful.
Find out which numbers / signs should be interchanged to get the correct equation among given alternatives.
In the questions given below the numbers in the figures are related. Identify their relationship and find the missing number.
The following questions are based on the given intersecting figures. Each figure represents a group.
Read the following questions carefully and find the answers.
In column 1 words are given, and their codes are given under column 2. Find the codes for given words.
In the following questions, a word is written according to some code. In the same way find the code for other given word.
The following questions consist of series of figures which are incomplete. In order to complete the series, select the correct option.
A sheet of paper is folded, punched and part of it is cut (shaded region). Select from the alternatives how it appears when the paper is unfolded.
In the following figures, a part of the figure is missing. Identify the missing part among the four alternatives given under each question.

In each of the given figures, there is a relationship between the first two figures. The same relation is between the next two figures, but one is missing. Find the missing figure from the given alternatives.
Assuming that the following statements are true, find the correct conclusion from the four alternatives.

questions.rule: These are prime numbers, in order.
questions.working: The prime number after 83 is 89. (91 = 7 × 13, 93 = 3 × 31 and 87 = 3 × 29 are not prime.)

questions.rule: Pairs of square and cube, counting down: 5², 5³, 4², 4³, 3², 3³, 2², 2³.
Each difference comes twice, and the differences grow by 4: +7, +7, +11, +11, +15, +15.
The letters a c b b c a repeat.
questions.working: a c b b c a | a c b b c a, so the boxes get c, c, c, b

questions.rule: Groups of four: p q r s, then the same letters starting one place later each time.
questions.working: pqrs | qrsp | rspq, so the boxes get r, q, p, p

questions.rule: The group y x x y repeats.
questions.working: yxxy | yxxy | yx, so the boxes get x, x, y, y

questions.rule: Multiply the number before, the number and the number after: 10 × 11 × 12 = 1320.
questions.working: 8 × 9 × 10 = 720, so the number is 9

questions.rule: Write the mixed number as one fraction, then write its top and bottom side by side: 4 1/5 = 21/5 → 215.
Take the square root and subtract 1: √1.21 = 1.1, and 1.1 − 1 = 0.1.
questions.note: As printed, only "square root, then subtract 1" gives an option (A, 1.5). The paper probably meant 1.21 : 1.1 (the square root), which would make the answer C, 2.5. Check the official key before showing this question.

questions.rule: The letters go back 1 and forward 1 in turn: M − 1 = L, A + 1 = B, S − 1 = R, K + 1 = L.
questions.working: L → K, O → P, C → B, K → L, D → C, O → P, W → V, N → O, so KPBLCPVO

questions.rule: Each letter moves forward one more place than the letter before: +1, +2, +3, +4, +5, +6.
questions.working: V + 1 = W, I + 2 = K, R + 3 = U, U + 4 = Y, S + 5 = X, so WKUYX

questions.rule: Twice each square number: 2 × 1², 2 × 2², 2 × 3², …
Two series take turns. 1st, 3rd, 5th… terms: 0, 1, 3, 6, 10 (+1, +2, +3, +4). 2nd, 4th, 6th… terms: the odd numbers 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
questions.working: The last two terms should be 10, 9 (10 from the first series, then 9 from the second). The pair 9, 10 is the wrong way round.

questions.rule: Divide by 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 in turn.
In the others both numbers are products of two numbers next to each other, and they share one: 72 = 8 × 9 and 56 = 7 × 8.
In the others the first two digits add up to 7: 5 + 2, 6 + 1, 4 + 3.
questions.working: 7123: 7 + 1 = 8 (it is also the only odd number)

questions.rule: In the others the letters move +5, −3, +7: G → L → I → P.
questions.working: S → X (+5) → U (−3) → Z is only +5, not +7

questions.rule: Add the letter places: HEC = 8 + 5 + 3 = 16, FBA = 9, LID = 25, all square numbers.
questions.working: OLH = 15 + 12 + 8 = 35, not a square number
questions.note: Two answers: the sums 16, 9, 35, 25 make C the odd one (35 is not a square), but the first step is −3 in HEC, OLH and LID and −4 in FBA, which makes B the odd one.

questions.rule: In the others the letters move +2, +3, +4: L → N → Q → U (after Z, count on from A).
questions.working: GILQ moves +2, +3, +5

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Karnataka, Bengaluru, Hyderabad?
questions.rule: Bengaluru is in Karnataka, so its circle is inside. Hyderabad is not in Karnataka, so its circle is outside.
questions.working: One circle inside a bigger one, and a third circle apart.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Metals, Iron, Carbon?
questions.rule: Iron is a metal, so its circle is inside. Carbon is not a metal, so its circle is outside.
questions.working: One circle inside a bigger one, and a third circle apart.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Humans, Singers, Musicians?
questions.rule: Singers and musicians are all humans, so both circles are inside. Some singers are musicians, so those two circles overlap.
questions.working: Two overlapping circles inside a big one.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Employees, Literates, Rich people?
questions.rule: Some employees are literate, some are rich, and some literates are rich, but none of the groups holds another.
questions.working: Three circles, each overlapping the other two.

questions.prompt: Find the missing number in the matrix.
questions.rule: In each row, the 2nd number × the 3rd number = 2 × the 1st number.

questions.prompt: Find the missing letter in the matrix.
questions.rule: Use the letter places. In each column, the sum of the three letters is 2, 3, then 4 times the top letter.

questions.prompt: Find the missing letter in the matrix.
questions.rule: Count the straight lines in each letter. The 1st column has letters of 2 lines (L, T), the 2nd of 3 lines (Z, H, K) and the 3rd of 4 lines (E, M, W).
questions.working: X is made of 2 lines. A, N and I (printed with its top and bottom bars) have 3.

questions.prompt: Find the missing number in the matrix.
questions.rule: In each row, the middle number is (1st × 3rd) + 1st + 3rd.

questions.prompt: Find the missing number in the matrix.
questions.rule: In each column, (top number)³ + (middle number)² = bottom number.

questions.prompt: Find the missing number in the matrix.
questions.rule: In each row, 2 × (letter place + number) = the 3rd number.

questions.prompt: Put the signs in place of each * in order, so that the statement is true. Which set of signs is right?
questions.rule: Try each set of signs in turn. Do × and ÷ first, then + and −, and compare the two sides.

questions.rule: Try each set of signs in turn. Do × and ÷ first (left to right), then + and −, and compare the two sides.

questions.prompt: Which two numbers or signs must be swapped to make the equation true?
questions.rule: Swap the two in each option, then work out both sides: × and ÷ first, then + and −.

questions.prompt: Which two numbers or signs must be swapped to make the equation true?
questions.rule: Swap the two in each option, then work out both sides: × and ÷ first, then + and −.

questions.prompt: Find how the numbers in the figures are related, and find the missing number.
questions.rule: The number inside is the average of the three corners: add them and divide by 3.

questions.prompt: Find how the numbers in the figures are related, and find the missing number.
questions.rule: Top × bottom + left × right gives the number inside.

questions.prompt: Find how the numbers in the figures are related, and find the missing number.
questions.rule: Numbers at the ends of one arrow add up to the same as the numbers at the ends of the other arrow.

questions.prompt: Find how the numbers in the figures are related, and find the missing number.
questions.rule: The three outer numbers add up to the square of the middle number.

questions.prompt: Find how the numbers in the figures are related, and find the missing number.
questions.rule: Divide the 3rd number by the 1st; the middle number is the square of the result.

questions.prompt: The number of businessmen who are not fishermen.
questions.rule: Businessmen are inside the rectangle, fishermen inside the circle. Add every number inside the rectangle but outside the circle.

questions.prompt: The total number of farmers who are businessmen.
questions.rule: Farmers are inside the triangle and businessmen inside the rectangle. Add every number inside both.

questions.prompt: The total number of fishermen who are both businessmen and farmers.
questions.rule: Find the part inside all three shapes: the circle, the rectangle and the triangle.
questions.working: Only 8 is inside all three.

questions.prompt: The number '7' represents the total number of:
questions.rule: 7 is inside the circle and outside both the rectangle and the triangle.
questions.working: So 7 counts the people who are fishermen and nothing else.

questions.prompt: A baby is born every two years in a family. If the family has 5 children in all and the sum of their ages is 40, what is the age of the eldest child?
questions.rule: Call the youngest child’s age x. The children are 2 years apart, so their ages are x, x + 2, x + 4, x + 6 and x + 8.
questions.working: 5x + 20 = 40 → x = 4, so the eldest is 4 + 8 = 12

questions.prompt: Introducing a man, Harsha said, "His only brother is the father of my daughter's father." How is that man related to Harsha?
questions.rule: Harsha's daughter's father is Harsha himself. So the man's only brother is Harsha's father.
questions.working: The man is the brother of Harsha's father, so he is Harsha's uncle.

questions.prompt: P is the father of Q, R is the son of P, S is the brother of T and T is the daughter of Q. Who is the grandfather of S?
questions.rule: T is Q's daughter and S is T's brother, so S is Q's child too.
questions.working: P is Q's father, so P is S's grandfather.

questions.prompt: If 6 February 2000 was a Sunday, what day of the week was 6 March 2001?
questions.rule: Count the odd days (days left over after whole weeks) from 6 February 2000 to 6 March 2001.
questions.working: 6 Feb 2000 to 6 Feb 2001 is 366 days (2000 is a leap year, and its 29 February comes in between): 2 odd days, so Tuesday. February 2001 has 28 days, exactly 4 weeks, so 6 March 2001 is also a Tuesday.

questions.prompt: A watch shows 10:30 pm. The minute hand points south. Which way does the hour hand point?
questions.rule: The minute hand points at 6, so 6 is south and 12 is north; then 3 is east and 9 is west.
questions.working: At 10:30 the hour hand is half-way between 10 and 11, between north (12) and west (9): north-west.

questions.prompt: Each word has its own code, but the code letters are not in the same order as the letters of the word. What is the code for AIR?
questions.rule: Compare words that share letters. F is in FRUIT, FUN and FOX, whose codes share only x, so F = x. In the same way U = m, N = z, O = y, X = b, R = c, I = p, A = n, T = s, S = k, E = j and L = o; in UMBRELLA, M and B are f and d.
questions.working: A = n, I = p, R = c, so npc

questions.prompt: Each word has its own code, but the code letters are not in the same order as the letters of the word. What is the code for LIST?
questions.rule: Compare words that share letters. F is in FRUIT, FUN and FOX, whose codes share only x, so F = x. In the same way U = m, N = z, O = y, X = b, R = c, I = p, A = n, T = s, S = k, E = j and L = o; in UMBRELLA, M and B are f and d.
questions.working: L = o, I = p, S = k, T = s, so opks

questions.prompt: Each word has its own code, but the code letters are not in the same order as the letters of the word. What is the code for BOSE?
questions.rule: Compare words that share letters. F is in FRUIT, FUN and FOX, whose codes share only x, so F = x. In the same way U = m, N = z, O = y, X = b, R = c, I = p, A = n, T = s, S = k, E = j and L = o; in UMBRELLA, M and B are f and d.
questions.working: O = y, S = k, E = j, and B is d (it is f or d, and only d fits an option), so dykj

questions.prompt: Each word has its own code, but the code letters are not in the same order as the letters of the word. What is the code for BURN?
questions.rule: Compare words that share letters. F is in FRUIT, FUN and FOX, whose codes share only x, so F = x. In the same way U = m, N = z, O = y, X = b, R = c, I = p, A = n, T = s, S = k, E = j and L = o; in UMBRELLA, M and B are f and d.
questions.working: B = d, U = m, R = c, N = z, so dmcz

questions.prompt: MACHINE is coded as PEFLLRH. How is PICTURE coded?
questions.rule: The letters move +3 and +4 in turn: M + 3 = P, A + 4 = E, C + 3 = F, H + 4 = L, …
questions.working: P + 3 = S, I + 4 = M, C + 3 = F, T + 4 = X, U + 3 = X, R + 4 = V, E + 3 = H, so SMFXXVH

questions.prompt: MASTER is coded as NZURHO. How is PERSON coded?
questions.rule: The letters move +1, −1, +2, −2, +3, −3: M → N, A → Z, S → U, T → R, E → H, R → O.
questions.working: P + 1 = Q, E − 1 = D, R + 2 = T, S − 2 = Q, O + 3 = R, N − 3 = K, so QDTQRK

questions.prompt: TABLE is coded as DKAZS. How is CHAIR coded?
questions.rule: Write the word backwards, then move each letter back one place: ELBAT → DKAZS.
questions.working: CHAIR backwards is RIAHC; each back one place: QHZGB

questions.prompt: FRUITS is coded as 1920921186. How is PIGEON coded?
questions.rule: Write the word backwards and put down the place of each letter: S = 19, T = 20, I = 9, U = 21, R = 18, F = 6.

questions.prompt: LION is coded as 150. How is GOAT coded?
questions.rule: Add the letter places and multiply by 3: L + I + O + N = 12 + 9 + 15 + 14 = 50, and 50 × 3 = 150.

questions.prompt: In the English alphabet, every other letter from A (A, C, E, …) is written as a capital letter and the rest as small letters. How is the third day after Monday written?
questions.rule: Letters in odd places (A = 1, C = 3, …) are capitals; letters in even places are small.
questions.working: The third day after Monday is Thursday: T (20) t, H (8) h, U (21) U, R (18) r, S (19) S, D (4) d, A (1) A, Y (25) Y, so thUrSdAY

questions.prompt: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Count one quarter of the square at a time, then the triangles made of halves of the square.
questions.working: Each of the two quarters with small lines has 13 triangles (9 small ones, the quarter itself and 3 made of several parts). The two plain quarters have 1 each. The two diagonals cut the square into halves, 4 more triangles: 13 + 13 + 1 + 1 + 4 = 32

questions.prompt: How many parallelograms are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Every two small triangles that share a side make a parallelogram; bigger ones are made of 4 small triangles.
questions.working: 8 made of 2 small triangles, and 4 made of 4 (two along the bottom row, and two slanting across both rows): 8 + 4 = 12

questions.prompt: How many semicircles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: A line right across a circle through its centre (a diameter) cuts it into 2 semicircles. A line that only goes from the centre to the edge does not.
questions.working: The big circle and the three small circles each have one diameter: 4 × 2 = 8. The two middle circles each have two diameters: 2 × 4 = 8. 8 + 8 = 16

questions.prompt: How many rectangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Pick 2 of the 5 up-and-down lines and 2 of the 4 across lines: each choice makes one rectangle.
questions.working: 5 lines give 10 pairs and 4 lines give 6 pairs: 10 × 6 = 60

questions.rule: The black wedge moves two of the eight parts clockwise each time, so the next one is at the top left.
questions.working: B and D have the wedge in the right place. The ⊗ goes back 3, 2, then 1 part, which points to D.
questions.note: The ⊙ goes 1 → 4 → 0 (of the eight parts), which points to a place none of the options shows. D fits the wedge and the ⊗ best; check the official key.

questions.rule: The corner shape gets one more side each time (triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon). The dot and the arrow move one quarter clockwise, and the arrow turns with them. The small triangle goes in and out of the top right corner.
questions.working: Next: a hexagon at the top left, the triangle in the top right corner, the arrow pointing up in the top right quarter and the dot in the bottom left quarter: B.

questions.rule: One more line goes across the hexagon each time (0, 1, 2, 3). The small circle shows in every other figure, and the small triangle moves clockwise round the corners.
questions.working: Next: three lines across, no circle, and the triangle in the bottom right corner: D.

questions.rule: One more of the eight triangles is black each time (1, 2, 3, 4), and each black part grows clockwise from where it starts.
questions.working: Figure 2 starts at the top, so figure 4 is the top and the next two triangles clockwise: the top-right half, D.

questions.rule: B: folded into a quarter, so each hole opens into four, mirrored in both fold lines, and the corner cut at the centre opens into a diamond.
questions.working: The hole near the top fold line makes two holes above and two below the centre, close to the middle. The hole near the right edge makes two on the right and two on the left, nearer the edge. The triangle cut from the corner, with its long side across, opens into a diamond (a square standing on its corner).

questions.rule: A: folded twice along the diagonals, so each hole opens into four, and the cut at the centre opens into a square.
questions.working: The two holes near the right edge open out into a pair of holes at each corner of the sheet. The small triangle cut at the centre has its cut edge upright; unfolded over the diagonals it makes a square with straight sides.

questions.rule: D: folded in half twice from left to right, so each hole opens into four, side by side.
questions.working: The hole at the top right corner of the strip opens into holes at both top corners and two near the top middle. The hole at the bottom left of the strip opens into two pairs along the bottom, a quarter of the way in from each side.

questions.rule: C: the two holes go through two layers (the folded tip and the sheet under it), and the sheet was folded in half first, so they open into 8 holes in two columns.
questions.working: Unfolding the tip gives 4 holes in the top half: two in a column a little left of the middle and two a little right. Unfolding the first fold mirrors them into the bottom half: 8 holes in two columns.

questions.prompt: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is opposite 4?
questions.rule: A number can’t be opposite any number it is seen next to.
questions.working: 5 is seen next to 2 and 3 (first view) and 1 and 6 (third view), so 5 is opposite the only number left, 4.

questions.prompt: Three positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is opposite 3?
questions.rule: A number can’t be opposite any number it is seen next to.
questions.working: 3 is seen next to 5 and 6 (first view) and 1 and 2 (third view), so 3 is opposite the only number left, 4.

questions.prompt: This sheet is folded into a cube. Which number will be opposite 4?
questions.rule: In a straight line of squares, the 1st and 3rd are opposite (one square between them). The column reads 2, 6, 4, 5.
questions.working: 2 and 4 are opposite (6 is between them), and 6 and 5 are opposite. So 4 is opposite 2.

questions.prompt: This sheet is folded into a cube. Which pair of faces will be opposite each other?
questions.rule: In a Z-shaped run of four squares, the two end squares are opposite.
questions.working: ● △ ■ ★ is a Z shape, so ● and ★ are opposite. (△ is opposite #, and ■ is opposite ◡.)

questions.rule: A: everything swaps left and right; nothing moves up or down.
questions.working: The arrow moves to the top right and points left, the half circle in the pentagon bulges to the right, the small circle moves to the upper left corner of the pentagon, and the spade moves to the bottom left with its other half shaded. B has the arrow on the wrong side.

questions.rule: B: every symbol is turned upside down (flipped top to bottom), in the same order.
questions.working: Water swaps top and bottom but not left and right, so the order stays @ ₹ $ & # ∽. The ₹ ends up with its bars underneath, like ≤, and the & has its tail at the top right. C reverses the order; D flips the ₹ and & the wrong way.

questions.rule: A: the bands along the top and bottom have ○ and the bands at the sides have ●.
questions.working: The missing quarter needs ● in its side band and ○ in its bottom band, both in their own band (C and D swap them; B has no line across the bottom). Its square matches the top left one turned half round.

questions.rule: C: the parts of the middle circle are black and white in turn.
questions.working: Going round the centre, black and white take turns, so the missing piece is black next to its top edge. C also keeps the two curved lines the other pieces have.

questions.rule: D: the figure looks the same turned half round, so the missing corner matches the top left corner turned half round.
questions.working: The top left block has a crossed square in its outer corner with a short line, and black triangles meeting at its middle. Turned half round: crossed square at the bottom right with the short line at the bottom, black triangles meeting in the middle. D has the short line; A does not.

questions.rule: B: each quarter, going clockwise, has a grey part, a white part and a thin striped part; each corner tip is white then black, going clockwise.
questions.working: So the missing quarter has grey along its top edge and the stripes along its left edge, a white tip on the right and a black tip at the bottom: B.

questions.rule: The shape is turned a quarter turn and a mirror copy is added beside it; the copy is shaded.
questions.working: The triangle stands on its point and a shaded copy joins it, making a diamond. So the two domes stand up as a small circle on a tall oval, left halves shaded: D.

questions.rule: The outer shape is turned upside down, but the small triangle inside stays upright, and the symbol in it is filled in.
questions.working: Pentagon → upside-down pentagon with the small triangle still upright and a filled star. So the triangle becomes upside down, the small triangle stays upright, and ○ becomes ●: D.

questions.rule: One more strip is added to the box, and the small shapes outside become half black.
questions.working: The box with 3 strips gets a 4th, and its two triangles become half black: B.

questions.rule: The outer shape goes, the lines across stay, and a black dot appears in each gap between them.
questions.working: The diamond goes, the + stays with 4 black dots. So the circle goes and the × stays with 4 black dots: C.

questions.prompt:
Statements:
(1) All horses are donkeys.
(2) Some donkeys are sheep.
Take the statements as true. Which conclusion follows?
questions.rule: Draw the groups as circles in every way the statements allow. A conclusion follows only if it is true in every drawing.
questions.working: The horses circle is inside the donkeys circle, so some donkeys are horses. The sheep circle only has to touch the donkeys circle somewhere, so nothing follows about horses and sheep.

questions.prompt:
Statement: Most of the members of that team are good players.
Which conclusion follows?

options.A: There are no bad players in that team.
options.B: All members of that team are good players.
options.C: Some members of that team are not good players.

questions.rule: "Most" means more than half, but not all.
questions.working: If most members are good players, the rest, some members, are not. Nothing is said about how the team performs.
